features.7ffdfbe91dc1: A full DAW with a room in it: up to four producers in one session, live, with no account and no server.
features.02a7818a6ee0: This page describes Freally Oscillate as it will be at version 1.0 — the rung the ladder ends on — and nothing planned after it.
features.89a259592591: Every figure is a count of what version 1.0 carries. Nothing is estimated and nothing is rounded up.
features.d6f79cef6f38: instruments and effects of its own
features.79067e736ea9: skins, each in light and dark
features.9df8f17ef9b5: Freally Secretarium plays the same instrument library as Freally MIDI Master: one library, pinned by both, rather than two copies that drift apart.
features.da9afac0d7b7: It is free today. All of it.
features.f997324cb19b: Every feature, for everyone. No paid tier, no trial that runs out, no licence key, no account and no in-app purchase.
features.22f1bb054323: What you make with it is yours. Oscillate's author claims no ownership of the projects, MIDI, audio or renders you create with it, and asks for no royalty and no credit.
features.45a1b4ecfbf5: A room with no server behind it
features.c3ea64baf32c: Send a room code to whoever you are working with and up to three other producers can join your session: their cursors on your timeline, chat, voice, camera tiles and screen share. Peer to peer, with no account and no server in the middle.
features.cb2c6359ccf6: <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd> takes back your last change and never somebody else's, even while their edits are arriving. The edit log behind it is also the room's sync, Session Rewind and the Split Sheet.
features.be31856f2db7: Hand one track to a collaborator and take it back with one key. While they hold it they are the only writer for it — including you — and that is enforced where edits are checked, not only in the interface.
features.d3a91a73c5cc: A beat battle mode in which each turn owns its own bars. The countdown is a countdown; the bars are the rule, so two computers can never disagree about whose edit was legal.
features.68481398e863: Who wrote what, derived from the edit log, with work anybody undid netted out. A starting point for a conversation about credit, not a legal document — and it says so.
features.2dc43d70f9ea: A take recorded in the room lands on everybody's timeline. A sample you bought is never sent: the room sends the reference, and a collaborator without the pack is told which samples they need.
features.b9277cfd1dc1: Unlimited audio and MIDI tracks, clips drawn from what they are, automation on every fader, pan and device control, comping, groups, markers, and tempo and time-signature maps. A pattern placed ten times is one pattern: edit it once and every placement changes, until you make one unique.
features.7e57d69f84a4: Draw a blade stroke across the arrangement and it splits every clip it crosses, the angle of the stroke setting the crossfade. Scrub the session's history like a video, and branch from any point in it.
features.8b5fc8a25fa8: Around ninety scales with highlighting, snapping and folding, ghost notes from any other clip, a velocity lane with a handle per note, lanes for how often each note plays and how far its velocity wanders, and a keyboard where one key can play a whole chord.
features.3b56c85ac1f3: Audio recording and a hardware MIDI keyboard on Windows, macOS and Linux. Takes stack under each other, you choose the parts you want, and the takes you did not choose are never deleted. Audio is written to disk as it arrives, so a crash costs the last block rather than the take.
features.0baacdf5d6c4: Your plugins, each in a process of its own
features.5fab46c33502: VST3 and CLAP. A plugin that crashes greys out its device and leaves the session running. Delay compensation is graph-wide and proved by a null test, and a plugin this machine does not have becomes a named placeholder, so a project opened somewhere else stays in time.
features.07e3bfdc40c6: Sixty-nine devices, among them Freally Secretarium and its 1 648 instruments. Each panel is drawn from the device's own description, so the number on a knob is the number the audio is using, and a device's settings copy as one line you can paste into a chat.
features.8d6419ade018: Six devices do what a plugin cannot, because a plugin cannot see the song it is in: a compressor already holding the chorus when it arrives, a gate that opens for a hit before it happens, a delay that empties into the bar line. None of the six adds latency.
features.4d7f4826526b: A strip per track with a fader, pan, mute, solo, the device rack and a meter drawn from the audio the engine actually produced. The Masking Radar names two tracks fighting for the same band and the frequency; the loudness panel shows integrated and short-term LUFS, the range and true peak against what each streaming service targets.
features.7d820a1cb209: Lyrics as a lane on the timeline, locked to the playhead and split into syllables, imported from .txt or .lrc and copied into the project — in type meant to be sung from across the room.
features.ef0a07e0d7a5: One shortcut renders a 1200×630 picture of the session to post. Session Timelapse rebuilds the whole session from its edit log as an animated picture with chapters — even a session nobody thought to record.
features.3ab5583a8c27: The companion folder writes stems and MIDI that any other DAW can open, lined up at bar 1, in the format, sample rate and bit depth you choose.
features.d65f870603be: Knobs, faders and buttons rendered in Blender, five skins in light and dark beside both themes, short interface sounds you can switch off, and eighteen languages with real right-to-left — the same look in every Freally app.
features.1c72614b8ea2: No account and no telemetry. It uses the network on three occasions only: a room you opened or joined, the address lookup while that room is set up, and an update check that is off until you switch it on. Crash reports stay on your disk unless you choose to send one.
features.ae2bbaa95738: No AI, enforced by the build
features.db3a0428cdec: No model, no inference, nothing generative. A build gate walks the dependency graph and fails on any inference runtime or model file, so it is a property of the build rather than a sentence on a website.

features.e5498b8a441d: The short version: every other product on that table asks for an account, and each asks for money for its full feature set. Two of them let several people edit one project — Pro Tools track by track through its cloud, Soundtrap live in its own cloud. Oscillate puts four producers in one arrangement live, peer to peer, with no account, and it is free today.
features.1889a974beb4: Compiled on 1 October 2026. A ✗ for a feature means it is not in that product's own feature lists, release notes or manual on that date. Products change, and this table describes them as they were then. Product names are the trademarks of their owners.
features.6977b748edc2: Why it is built the way it is
features.662d60837a2d: No server, so nothing to switch off
features.85567c225aa3: A room code is the connection offer itself. With no server there is nothing to keep running, nothing to pay for and nothing anybody can turn off — which is also why a room holds four producers and not forty: every peer sends to every other peer.
features.d2a4cd186952: Every edit is an operation in one log. Undo, the room's sync, Session Rewind and the Split Sheet are four readings of it, which is why your undo can be yours alone and why credit can be derived rather than typed in.
features.af0df7623348: A crash is one device, not the session
features.600105cd00bc: Every hosted plugin runs in a process of its own, and the application itself cannot even load one. A plugin that falls over greys out its device, and the transport keeps playing.
features.908ec1ae94d2: The number you see is the number in the audio
features.b6fc9acbd76d: Meters are drawn from what the engine produced, a knob's readout from the value the DSP is using, and a measurement that fell behind says so. Nothing on screen is a prediction.
features.70a55e97f377: Your projects, audio and MIDI leave your computer only when you are in a room with somebody — and then they go straight to the people in it, not through anybody's cloud.
features.735112899b1c: Stated plainly, because a feature list that hides its gaps is not worth reading. Everything above is what version 1.0 is planned to have, and this is what still stands between here and there.
features.5ea6fea0e17d: Two more rungs of features: 0.6.0, identity — the Lyric Lane, Session Timelapse, session cards and the credits page — and 0.6.5, the family look and the right instruments: the Blender-rendered hardware, the five skins, the interface sounds and one instrument library with Freally MIDI Master.
features.423615e1b37c: A public beta, then a release candidate hardened against what the beta finds.

features.e1158416235c: Every rung is on the road to 1.0.
features.7d48e18b39c1: Host AU or VST2 plugins. It hosts VST3 and CLAP.
features.a1eea7d00cdd: Use ASIO. On Windows the low-latency path is WASAPI exclusive, and Oscillate tells you which mode you actually got.
features.1bcf2a5c1071: Hold more than four producers in a room. The fifth connection is where an ordinary home upload gives out.
features.37e6fd7fe6f5: Relay a connection that will not form. Roughly one in ten will not without a relay in the middle; Oscillate names the cause, and Settings takes your own relay.
features.d32646eadd7e: Share a screen from macOS. Screen share is Windows and Linux; on macOS the button is absent and says why.
features.5590fbf60cd6: Carry pitch bend, the mod wheel or pressure from a hardware keyboard. Notes, velocity and the sustain pedal are carried.
features.3b50036d04c0: No beta on this page, no preview build, no early access. Until 1.0.0 the honest answer to “where do I get it” is not yet.
